headline: Fog clears to a sunny low-to-mid 70s Thursday; a weak front brings rain Friday into Saturday, then a cooler, possibly frosty Sunday.
summary: As of the last discussion Thursday morning, dense fog was lingering in parts of western Washington, including the lowlands of western Skagit and northwestern Snohomish Counties (the Everett and Marysville area), the Washington coast, and the waters of Puget Sound. Fog advisories ran until noon or 1 PM, and forecasters expected it to clear later in the morning. Fog was expected to be less widespread than in recent days. After that, high pressure brings sunshine and afternoon highs in the low to mid 70s. A weak front then arrives Friday into Saturday with a round of rain across western Washington and breezy southwest winds around Puget Sound. Winds are expected to be stronger in the Strait of Juan de Fuca. Rain totals should be about a quarter to a half inch in the Cascades and a few hundredths to a tenth of an inch elsewhere. Snow levels drop to around 4,500-5,000 ft Friday night into Saturday, bringing an inch of snow or less, mainly in the North Cascades. Saturday night into Sunday turns drier and cooler. Sunday morning lows are mostly in the upper 30s to low 40s, and some Cascade valleys could drop to around freezing, which matters for gardens and frost-sensitive plants. That freeze risk is only about 30%, so it is possible but not likely. Highs midweek are in the low to mid 60s, with another chance of light rain Tuesday. Forecasters are fairly confident in the front and the cooler pattern behind it. After Wednesday, computer models disagree on whether the cool, unsettled pattern lingers or high pressure returns. On the water, a Small Craft Advisory covers the central and eastern Strait of Juan de Fuca from 2 PM Thursday to 3 AM Friday. A Gale Watch for the coastal waters and the Strait runs from late Thursday night through Friday evening, and gale-force gusts are possible but not certain.
changes: The forecast for rain, wind, and the cooler weekend stayed essentially the same all day. The main change was the fog: the morning discussions had Dense Fog Advisories until 10 AM, and by 9:36 AM they were extended to noon or 1 PM and covered the Everett and Marysville lowlands.
